High-noon top-light from a single overhead key, driving short crisp shadows beneath every snow-plate cap and rock-brick ledge, saturated contrast across the full vista, a clear-day diorama mood.

God-rays through a cloud-gap, a warm built shaft from trans-yellow tiles and a focused hot zone breaking the round-plate cloud-bank, spotlighting one valley patch while surrounding bricks stay cooler.
Warm low-sun gild from a shallow front-right angle, amber light raking the upper slope-brick faces and gilding each protruding stud while the valley-floor bricks sink into cool blue shadow.

Cool shadowed-valley with lit summits, deep blue-grey shadow pooling across the low terrain bricks while only the highest snow-plate peaks catch a warm focused key, strong tonal separation across levels.
Alpenglow rose on the snow-caps, a soft pink-warm diffused source aimed at the white-plate summits while the lower brick range falls into a deepening blue-hour shadow, quiet and majestic.
Overcast soft-even wash from a broad diffused overhead panel, shadowless pale light revealing every brick-course detail and texture uniformly across the diorama, a contemplative moody plateau vista.
Dawn first-light from a low front angle catching only the single highest peak-plate, one warm bright summit glowing against an otherwise blue-toned unlit brick range, day arriving at the top first.

Dramatic single-shaft spotlight, one hard warm beam as if through a ridge notch, illuminating one valley zone sharply while surrounding slope-brick terrain stays in cool theatrical shadow, intense focal depth.

Raking cross-light from the right edge, a hard source travelling horizontally across the diorama face, every brick row casting its neighbour into shadow, emphasising horizontal strata-courses with maximum plastic relief.
Dual-rim backlight from two rear corners, both ridge edges glowing simultaneously, the full back-range silhouetted and the central valley cut deep and cool between two bright plateau outlines.

Steep front-low key angled upward from below the baseplate, underlighting the brick cliff-faces to reverse their shadow, giving the terrain an eerie inverted relief across every protruding stud course.
Split warm-cool side-light, warm amber from the left and cool blue from the right, each half of the brick terrain receiving an opposing tonal key, the ridge-line acting as the sharp divide.

Narrow slit-light from a hard masked source above, a single bright band crossing the mid-range brick slope diagonally, casting everything above and below that band into relative darkness, geometric and stark.
Soft side-fill from a wide diffused panel at the right, gentle graduated shadow-fall across the slope-bricks producing delicate low-contrast relief, a hazy afternoon plateau mood without harsh edges.
